item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police have launched a murder investigation following the discovery of a woman’s body at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. The victim has been named as Vera. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the property on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.
A post-mortem examination is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon. Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee has described the death as an isolated incident. Authorities are asking anyone with information to contact them online or by calling 101, quoting Operation Emeth.

item.title: Looking back at local news from November 1996
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at local news from November 1996
We are taking a look back at the headlines from late November 1996. In Hockwold, darts players completed a 12-hour charity marathon, raising funds for the cancer ward at Addenbrooke’s Hospital. Meanwhile, in West Lynn, the Reverend Andrew Davey voiced criticism over a local initiative to fund two part-time special constables. The scheme, intended to tackle vandalism, relied on community contributions and business donations, leading the rector to question why residents should pay twice for policing services.
Elsewhere in the region, West Norfolk councillors approved an £835,000 plan for a new Red Cross centre in Downham, while receivers were appointed at the Saddlebow Road speedway stadium in King's Lynn.

item.title: Local editors warn government over online news plans
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Local editors warn government over online news plans
Editors from across the UK, including the editor of the Fenland Citizen, have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group argues that the suggested prominence regime is unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism by distorting the news marketplace.
The letter highlights fears that the policy could lead to fewer local news sources for communities. Instead, the editors are calling for alternative support, such as ensuring fair payment from digital platforms and increasing government advertising spend in local titles. The signatories believe these changes are necessary to protect the sustainability of the local news ecosystem.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/local-editors-across-uk-warn-culture-secretary-over-unworka-9492933/

item.title: Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
An 18-year-old man has been handed a suspended prison sentence after a dangerous police pursuit across Norfolk. Ellis Rabey-Prosser, of Mildenhall, reached speeds of 100mph and drove the wrong way around a roundabout in Swaffham during the incident on October 6. The pursuit concluded when he crashed into a lamppost at the Hardwick roundabout in King’s Lynn.
Rabey-Prosser pleaded guilty to multiple charges, including dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. At Norwich Magistrates’ Court, he received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. He has also been disqualified from driving for a further two years and must pay £227 in costs. Police confirmed the driver had altered his vehicle's number plate before the pursuit began.

Local editors warn government over online news plans
Editors from across the UK have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group, which includes editors from local titles across the country, warns that the current proposals are unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism.

item.description:

National operator First Bus acquires King’s Lynn company Lynx
The King’s Lynn-based bus operator Lynx has been acquired by the national firm First Bus. The move aims to expand the company's network across North and West Norfolk. Lynx, which was founded in 2014, currently manages 25 routes with a fleet of 38 vehicles and 80 staff members.
The existing management team will remain in place, and Lynx will continue to operate as a separate unit within the First Bus portfolio. Founders Julian Patterson, Andy Warnes, and Steve Challis stated that the partnership will help protect the business while providing access to national investment and expertise. First Bus says it intends to build on the existing reputation of the service to encourage further bus travel in the region.

item.title: New coffee shop to open in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New coffee shop to open in King’s Lynn
A new branch of Esquires The Organic Coffee Co. is scheduled to open in King’s Lynn this Wednesday, November 25. The café is located on the High Street at the site of the former Burtons and Coneys menswear store.
Signage has been visible at the premises for several weeks, and preparations are now nearing completion with furniture and lighting installed. The franchise, which already operates a site in Swaffham, specialises in organic and Fairtrade coffee. This opening follows the brand’s announcement in October that it would be expanding into the town.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/new-town-centre-coffee-shop-set-to-open-on-wednesday-9492502/

item.title: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police remain at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech following the death of a 61-year-old woman. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and is currently in police custody.
Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the major crime unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that officers are not searching for anyone else. Residents with information are encouraged to contact the police online or by calling 101, quoting Operation Emeth. Investigations at the site are ongoing.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/police-remain-at-suspected-murder-scene-after-61-year-old-wo-9492417/
